title: Frontend: All Pairs Shortest Path (Floyd-Warshall Algorithm)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind All Pairs Shortest Path (Floyd-Warshall Algorithm). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({count,edges}) for directed weighted edges [from,to,weight]. Return all-pairs distance matrix, null for unreachable. Diagonals start at zero; keep smallest parallel edge. Any negative cycle throws Negative cycle.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Initialize diagonal distances to zero and each direct edge to the minimum parallel-edge weight.
alternativeApproaches: Maintain a next-hop matrix for path reconstruction and mark pairs whose result is unbounded by a reachable negative cycle.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Disconnected pair; parallel edge; negative edge.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
